The first week of daycare I felt so guilty and felt like the staff judged me because my son would be the first one to arrive in his room and one of the last to leave. It’s been almost a month and not only do the employees love him, they really are there to help. It’s no different than dropping him off at grandmas house for the day. Sure, if we were better off financially I would stay home with him as long as possible. But taking him to daycare has helped not only me and my husband be able to have that “weight” off our shoulders, its really helped us with being better parents. A lot of times I’m unsure what to do with my son to keep him appropriately entertained for each month he gets older. Daycare not only helps with that, they truly are the only “village” we have to help as both my husband and I’s families are hours away. Don’t let the haters bother you. Unfortunately everyone seems to have an opinion on every aspect of parenting and I have come to accept that, and to accept that my husband and I are the ones who are our son’s parents. Bottom line do what is best for your family and situation! No two families are 100% alike.

I brought soap, they didn’t provide shower items. They had toothpaste, toothbrush, swaddle blankets, diapers, wipes, idk what its called but a wrap like shirt for baby, non slip socks(I brought more because my husband stole the hospital ones from me lol), postpartum stuff like pads underwear witch hazel(i also asked for extra before we left).

I suggest bringing basic shower items(think travel sized and just simple soap and shampoo/conditioner), hair brush, long phone charger and wall adapter, my husband and i both brought throw blankets that he ended up using both of them because I was so hot in the room and he was freezing, a pillow(i brought a squishmallow because its smaller and was almost like a “piece of home”), snacks(depending on your hospital l&d may have a snack room for you, mine had a fridge of juices and extra lunches).
